newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's Prodi to face confidence test after vote.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Prodi to face confidence test after vote.

text.p: Italy's President Oscar Luigi Scalfaro told Prime Minister Romano Prodi to put his government to a confidence test after his hard left ally opposed him in parliamentary vote to send a military force to Albania.

A statement issued by Scalfaro after a one-hour meeting with Prodi said the President had asked the prime minister to "promote the indispensable political clarification" through a statement to parliament.
Political sources said that Prodi would speak to the Senate at 1230 (1030 GMT) before making a statement to the lower house of parliament in the afternoong.
A confidence vote would be held in the Senate in the late evening, the sources said. It was not immediately clear when the lower chamber would hold a confidence vote.

Prodi, facing the stiffest political challenge in 11 months in office, staved off an immediate government crisis when the centre-right opposition Freedom Alliance said it would vote with his centre-left coalition on a joint motion to deploy an Italian-led multinational force in Albania.

The motion passed by 503 votes to 85 but the opposition exacted a high price for siding with the government, forcing Prodi into a humiliating admission in parliament that he was not able to muster a majority of his own on the policy.
